title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: Work IQ REST API for custom apps, billed in Copilot Credits
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap details, billing prerequisite, Copilot Credits licensing and spending-policy controls are supported by Microsoft sources. It accurately distinguishes the REST conversation API from MCP action capabilities and reports the differing service-principal provisioning descriptions.

claims.claim: Administrators can monitor Work IQ consumption and spending at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost management.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft admin center, Copilot > Cost management, admins can monitor Copilot Credit consumption and manage spending associated with the supported services such as Cowork, running apps hosted on the Copilot Managed Runtime, and Work IQ API.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; controls[1].note; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Spending policies define access and spending limits without reserving or allocating credits.
claims.quote: Spending policies are limit-based controls and don't reserve or allocate Copilot Credits to users or groups.

claims.claim: When users hit the policy limit they lose access until credits reset on the first of the month.
claims.quote: When users hit the limit, they lose access to agents and services for the rest of the month until credits reset on the first of the month.

claims.claim: Creating a spending policy requires Billing Administrator or Global Administrator.
claims.quote: Creating a spending policy also requires the Billing Administrator or Global Administrator directory role at runtime.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The policy page requires at least 2,000 credits per user per month for the monthly user budget limit.
claims.quote: Monthly budget limit for users: Set at least 2,000 credits per user per month

claims.claim: The enablement page documents one-time manual provisioning of the Work IQ service principal.
claims.quote:
~5 minutes, one-time per organization.
This section creates the Work IQ service principal in your organization, which provisions the Work IQ resource so your applications can request tokens for it.

claims.claim: The MCP overview says the principal is created automatically on first use, with manual provisioning potentially needed beforehand.
claims.quote: The Work IQ service principal is created automatically in the tenant when you use Work IQ for the first time. In some corner cases, such as configuring Work IQ MCP policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center before any MCP use in the tenant, the service principal might not exist yet

claims.claim: The enablement page lists a usage-based billing plan with an Azure subscription and resource group as a prerequisite.
claims.quote: A usage-based billing plan set up in Copilot Studio with an Azure subscription and resource group assigned.

claims.claim: The Claude walkthrough requires an identity-based policy covering its users and the Work IQ API service.
claims.quote: After configuring usage-based billing, create or update an identity-based spending policy covering the approved users and the Work IQ API for custom apps and agents service.

claims.claim: Auto-apply new services is enabled by default in spending policies.
claims.quote: By default, the Auto-apply new services toggle is selected for spending policies.

claims.claim: Policy service selection is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > spending policy > Agents and services.
claims.quote: go to Copilot > Cost Management. Select the Configuration tab. Select the spending policy you want to edit. The spending policy details fly-out opens, where you can modify its settings. This includes: Scope; Agents and services; Billing method; Spending limits

claims.quote: go to Copilot > Cost Management. Select the Configuration tab. Select the spending policy you want to edit. The spending policy details fly-out opens, where you can modify its settings. This includes: Scope; Agents and services; Billing method; Spending limits

claims.claim: Disabling the last enabled service in a policy is refused with HTTP 409 atLeastOneServiceRequired.
claims.quote: Disabling the last enabled service is refused with a `409 atLeastOneServiceRequired` response.

claims.claim: Setting state to disabled removes the service from policy participation while retaining its service-setting entry.
claims.quote: Setting `state` to `disabled` is the removal semantic; the entry is retained in that state, and the collection has no `DELETE`.

claims.claim: Both spending-policy PATCH operations support delegated work or school accounts only, not application permissions.
claims.quote:
| Delegated (work or school account) | CopilotCostManagement-Policy.ReadWrite.All | Not supported. |

claims.claim: Both spending-policy PATCH operations require CopilotCostManagement-Policy.ReadWrite.All.
claims.quote: | Delegated (work or school account) | CopilotCostManagement-Policy.ReadWrite.All | Not supported. |

claims.claim: Excluding Work IQ API from one policy does not exclude it from other applicable policies, including the default policy.
claims.quote: Review all applicable policies, including the default policy. Excluding a service from one policy doesn't exclude it from other policies.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy controls in the Microsoft 365 admin center are documented for MCP tool requests.
claims.quote:
This article focuses on how policy governance applies to Work IQ MCP tool requests.
In the Microsoft 365 admin center, tenant administrators can turn Work IQ MCP policy on or off for the tenant.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents tenant-wide blocking for the Work IQ MCP server.
claims.quote: Block Work IQ MCP tenant-wide only when you intend to stop it for the entire tenant.

claims.claim: The connectors page says administrators can enable or disable connector participation in Work IQ paths through tenant-level policies.
claims.quote: Administrators can explicitly enable or disable connector participation in Work IQ paths through tenant-level policies.

claims.claim: The listed controls govern consumption within spending policies rather than directly blocking the REST endpoint.
claims.quote:
Spending policies control access and spending limits; they don't reserve or allocate credits for a workload, user, or group.
Excluding a service from one policy doesn't exclude it from other policies.

claims.claim: Custom app access requires an application configured with the delegated permission, rather than starting automatically.
claims.quote: Consent authorizes the client application to request those permissions on behalf of users. It doesn't grant users access to Microsoft 365 content they couldn't otherwise access, enable billing, or override Work IQ tenant policy.
